statement: Express $\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x$ in the form $R\cos(x+\alpha)$ with $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, and hence solve $\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x=1$ for $0\le x<2\pi$.
solution: $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x=2(\tfrac12\cos x-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin x)=2\cos(x+\tfrac{\pi}{3})$. The equation becomes $2\cos(x+\tfrac{\pi}{3})=1$, so $\cos(x+\tfrac{\pi}{3})=\tfrac12$. For $x\in[0,2\pi)$, $x+\tfrac{\pi}{3}\in[\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{7\pi}{3})$, giving $x+\tfrac{\pi}{3}=\tfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\tfrac{5\pi}{3}$, i.e. $x=0$ or $x=\tfrac{4\pi}{3}$.
